title: Cabin-crew "selection" after a phone interview with uniform and training fees vs. airline recruiter inviting to an in-person assessment
summary: A recruiter from NeelGagan Airways calls an applicant for cabin crew. In the fraud case, the recruiter declares the applicant "selected" on the strength of a short phone conversation and asks for uniform, grooming, and training charges to a personal account before an appointment letter is sent. In the legitimate case, the recruiter invites the applicant to an in-person assessment day, lists the documents to bring, and states that the airline charges nothing at any stage.

shared_setting.recipient_profile: a 19–27-year-old applicant with Class 12 or a degree; details sampled at generation.
other_facts: Role: trainee cabin crew, base [CITY], stipend during training then salary [AMOUNT_1] (₹30,000–₹55,000 per month).
Both calls mention grooming standards, training, uniform, and documents.

fraud.label_rationale: The caller confirms selection without any face-to-face assessment and asks the applicant to pay for uniform and training to an individual's account before the appointment letter.
fraud.caller_objective: Collect the charges and later ones ("insurance", "agreement"); there is no job.
stable_facts: Charges: [AMOUNT_2] (₹8,000–₹30,000), itemised as uniform, grooming kit, and training registration.
Paid to [ACCT_LAST4] or [UPI_ID_1] in an individual's name.
Appointment letter "released within 24 hours of payment" from a free email address.

Documents to bring: ID proof, educational certificates, passport-size photos, passport if available.
Uniform and training are provided by the airline; a pre-employment medical is arranged and paid by the airline after selection.

cooperative.fraud: Agrees to pay and asks for the account details
cooperative.legitimate: Confirms attendance and asks about dress code for the assessment

clarifying.fraud: Asks whether the uniform cost can be cut from salary
clarifying.legitimate: Asks about height and grooming requirements

resistant.fraud: Says they want to attend an in-person interview before paying
resistant.legitimate: Says the date clashes with an exam and asks for another

suspicious.fraud: Says airlines do not charge candidates and asks for an official email
suspicious.legitimate: Asks how to confirm the call is from NeelGagan

fraud: caller offers "half now" and applicant declines
legitimate: caller tells a suspicious applicant to check the careers page and wait for the official email.

caller_continuation_limits: The fraud caller may reduce the amount, add urgency, or promise refund on joining. They must not switch to OTPs, bank logins, or app installs. The legitimate caller must not ask for any payment after the branch.

must_preserve: role, base, and salary identical across cases
_F selection-by-phone plus payment to an individual's account at turn 7
_L in-person assessment and explicit no-fee statement
must_not_emit: body-related remarks beyond neutral grooming standards

ambiguities: Uniform", "training", and "medical" appear in both cases; none is evidence.
A phone call from the airline is normal; being declared selected after only a phone call is supporting evidence, not the core evidence.
Distinct from jr_01: this family impersonates the employer itself (not an agency) and ties the payment to post-"selection" items.

evidence_references.claim: At least one major Indian airline charges no money for interviews or recruitment and tells candidates not to pay for registration, uniform, training, or joining deposits (CJ04)
The same airline advises not accepting offers after phone-only interviews without a face-to-face meeting (CJ05)
Upfront payment is a red flag in fake job schemes (C11)
